'''Jacqueline Irwin''' (née '''Van Egmond'''; born January 3, 1962), an American [[politician]], is the current [[United States House of Representatives|US House of Representatives]] elect for District 26.  Prior to winning the House seat she  served  in the [[California State Assembly]]. She is a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] representing the [[California's 42nd State Assembly district|42nd Assembly district]], having previously represented the 44th. Before being elected to the Assembly in 2014, Irwin worked as a [[Systems engineering|systems engineer]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]] and [[Teledyne]], then served as a two-term mayor and three-term city councilmember in [[Thousand Oaks, California|Thousand Oaks]]. She is currently the Democratic nominee for {{ushr|CA|26}} in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections|2026 election]].

== Early life and education ==
Irwin was born in the [[Tarzana, Los Angeles|Tarzana]] neighborhood of [[Los Angeles, California|Los Angeles]] to [[Netherlands|Dutch]] immigrants John and Barbara Van Egmond, and grew up in the [[Woodland Hills, Los Angeles|Woodland Hills]] neighborhood.<ref name=vcstar2008>{{cite news|url=http://archive.vcstar.com/news/thousand-oaks-mayoral-debut-ep-374453707-352688341.html/|title=Thousand Oaks mayoral debut|work=[[Ventura County Star]]|first=Rachel|last=Mcgrath|date=January 11, 2008|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> She graduated with a systems engineering degree from the [[University of California, San Diego]], where she was an [[Academic All-America|Academic All American]] swimmer.<ref name=vcstar>{{cite news|url=https://archive.vcstar.com/news/elections/irwin-plunges-into-partisan-politics-with-problem-solving-approach-ep-664043730-351167821.html/|title=Irwin plunges into partisan politics with problem-solving approach|work=[[Ventura County Star]]|first=Timm|last=Herdt|date=October 9, 2014|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating from UC San Diego, Irwin worked as an engineer for three years at the [[Applied Physics Laboratory|Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Lab]], then for five years at [[Teledyne]].<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710152101/http://www.mpacorn.com/news/2014-01-10/Community/Jacqui_Irwin_puts_name_in_the_running_to_lead_44th.html|archive-date=July 10, 2015|url=http://www.mpacorn.com/news/2014-01-10/Community/Jacqui_Irwin_puts_name_in_the_running_to_lead_44th.html|title=Jacqui Irwin puts name in the running to lead 44th District|work=Moorpark Acorn|date=January 10, 2014|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> In 2003, Irwin was appointed to the Thousand Oaks Planning Commission, ran for City Council the following year, and became mayor of Thousand Oaks in 2008.<ref name=vcstar2008 />

In 2014, Irwin successfully ran as a Democrat in the race to represent [[California's 44th State Assembly district]], defeating Republican opponent Rob McCoy.<ref name=cbs2014>{{cite news|url=https://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2014/11/12/democratic-rep-julia-brownley-wins-re-election/|title=Democratic Rep. Julia Brownley Wins Re-Election|publisher=KCAL 9 CBS Los Angeles|date=November 12, 2014|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>  Irwin has been reelected four times in 2016, 2018, 2020, and most recently 2022 in the new [[California's 42nd State Assembly district]] after redistricting occurred.

=== Legislative tenure ===
Irwin is the chair of the Assembly Committee on Revenue and Taxation,<ref>{{cite web |title=California State Assembly Committee on Revenue and Taxation |url=https://arev.assembly.ca.gov/ |website=California State Assembly}}</ref> and the Assembly Select Committee on Cybersecurity,<ref>{{cite web |title=Assembly Select Committee on Cybersecurity |url=https://www.assembly.ca.gov/selectcommitteeoncybersecurity |website=California State Assembly |access-date=January 29, 2020 |archive-date=January 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129065137/https://www.assembly.ca.gov/selectcommitteeoncybersecurity |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the Assembly Select Committee on Gasoline Supply and Pricing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-20 |title=California lawmakers promise relief with probe into 'gas price gouging' |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2022/06/20/california-lawmakers-promise-relief-with-new-select-committee-on-gas-price-gouging |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=The Mercury News |language=en-US}}</ref> She also serves on the Committees on Agriculture, Business & Professions, Higher Education, and Privacy and Consumer Protection.<ref>{{cite web |title=Committees |url=https://a44.asmdc.org/committees |website=Official Website- Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin}}</ref> She previously served as chair of the Assembly Committee on Military and Veterans Affairs from 2014–2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biography {{!}} Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin Representing the 44th California Assembly District |url=https://a44.asmdc.org/biography |access-date=2022-04-01 |website=a44.asmdc.org}}</ref>

Irwin has also been appointed to other significant roles including the Governor's Military Council,<ref>{{cite web |title=About the Council |url=https://militarycouncil.ca.gov/m_aboutthecouncil/ |website=Governor’s Military Council}}</ref> and as co-chair of the [[National Conference of State Legislatures|National Conference of State Legislature]]’s Task Force on Cybersecurity.<ref>{{cite web |title=Task Force on Cybersecurity |url=https://www.ncsl.org/ncsl-in-dc/task-forces/task-force-on-cybersecurity.aspx |website=National Conference of State Legislatures}}</ref>

==== 2015–2016 session ====
During her first term in office, Irwin passed significant legislation. Irwin improved the cybersecurity of the state by mandating state agencies undergo independent security assessments,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Raths |first1=David |title=Legislating Cybersecurity: Lawmakers Recognize Their Responsibility with Cyberthreats |url=https://www.govtech.com/security/Legislating-Cybersecurity-Lawmakers-Recognize-Their-Responsibility-with-Cyberthreats.html |publisher=Government Technology |date=October 11, 2016}}</ref> she banned [[Alcohol powder|powdered alcohol]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Press Release- Governor Signs Ban on Sale of Powdered Alcohol |url=https://alcoholjustice.org/images/9-28-16_IrwinPR_AB1554_BL.pdf |website=Alcohol Justice}}</ref> expanded the ability of [[University of California]] research to be turned into real-world applications,<ref>{{cite web |title=State invests $22 million in UC entrepreneurship, innovation to drive California economy |url=https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/press-room/CA-invests-22-million-uc-entrepreneurship-innovation-drive-california-economy |website=University of California |date=30 September 2016 |publisher=University of California Office of the President}}</ref> and worked with Attorney General [[Kamala Harris]] to create the OpenJustice Web portal to provide better access to criminal justice data.<ref>{{cite web |title=Attorney General Kamala D. Harris Applauds Passage of OpenJustice Data Act of 2016 in California State Legislature |date=30 August 2016 |url=https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-applauds-passage-openjustice-data-act-2016 |publisher=California Department of Justice}}</ref>

==== 2017–2018 session ====
During her second term in office, Irwin helped secure critical funding for infrastructure projects in Ventura County, including $68.6 million for a grade separation project at Rice Avenue in [[Oxnard, California]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Mike |title=Officials laud funding for planned bridge in Oxnard that they say will save lives |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/local/communities/oxnard/2018/05/22/officials-laud-long-awaited-planned-bridge-oxnard/607854002/ |publisher=Ventura County Star |date=May 22, 2018}}</ref> and $9.5 million for emergency wastewater treatment facility repairs in Oxnard, California.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Leung |first1=Wendy |title=Assemblywoman Irwin secures $9.5 million for Oxnard sewer plant repairs |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/2018/07/17/assemblywoman-irwin-secures-9-5-million-oxnard-sewer-plant/768140002/ |work=Ventura County Star |date=July 17, 2018}}</ref>

She continued her work passing significant cybersecurity legislation, enacting into law the first ever security requirement for Internet of Things devices.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Douglas |first1=Theo |title=California Governor Approves Bills Tightening Security, Privacy of IoT Devices |url=https://www.govtech.com/applications/Two-Bills-Before-California-Governor-Would-Tighten-Security-Privacy-of-IoT-Devices.html |work=Government Technology |date=September 28, 2018}}</ref> Irwin also significantly changed how [[California Community Colleges]] approached [[remedial education]] in an effort to get students into transfer level courses.<ref>{{cite web |title=What is AB 705? |url=https://assessment.cccco.edu/ab-705-implementation |website=California Community Colleges}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Trust students, not tests, to open pathway to community college success |url=https://edsource.org/2018/trust-students-not-tests-to-open-pathway-to-community-college-success/596996 |work=Ed Source |date=May 2, 2018}}</ref>

==== 2019–2020 session ====
In 2019 Irwin focused heavily on gun violence prevention legislation in response to the [[Thousand Oaks shooting|Borderline Shooting]] in Thousand Oaks, California. Her legislation strengthened [[Gun violence restraining order|Gun Violence Restraining Orders (GVROs)]], in part by allowing them to extend up to five years. She also required law enforcement agencies to have policies about using GVROs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Governor Gavin Newsom Signs Gun Violence Prevention Legislation |date=11 October 2019 |url=https://www.gov.ca.gov/2019/10/11/governor-gavin-newsom-signs-gun-violence-prevention-legislation/ |publisher=Office of Governor Gavin Newsom}}</ref> Irwin also secured $3 million to support local law enforcement efforts to recover firearms from individuals listed in the Armed and Prohibited Possessors System.<ref>{{cite web |title=Assemblymember Irwin works to secure state funding for crucial Ventura County programs |url=https://a44.asmdc.org/press-releases/20190614-assemblymember-irwin-works-secure-state-funding-crucial-ventura-county |publisher=Office of Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin |access-date=January 29, 2020 |archive-date=January 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129065135/https://a44.asmdc.org/press-releases/20190614-assemblymember-irwin-works-secure-state-funding-crucial-ventura-county |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In October 2019, Irwin pulled out of attending a fundraising event for the family of an officer killed in the Borderline shooting.<ref name="vcstarbluebowl">{{cite news|url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/local/communities/conejo-valley/2019/10/02/borderline-shooting-fundraiser-benefit-slain-deputy-postponed/3841717002/|title=Fundraiser to honor sheriff's deputy killed in Borderline shooting postponed|work=Ventura County Star|first=Mike|last=Harris|date=October 2, 2019|access-date=January 18, 2020}}</ref> After the Ventura County Sheriff's Office also withdrew from the fundraiser, citing a policy of non-participation in political events, the event was postponed indefinitely.<ref name="vcstarbluebowl" /> An organizer of the event was later arrested in Florida for felony violations of charitable solicitation law and misusing charitable funds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seaver |first=Matthew |date=2022-06-22 |title=Collier County fallen officers charity founder arrested, accused of misusing donations |url=https://www.winknews.com/2022/06/22/fallen-officers-charity-founder-arrested-accused-of-misusing-donations/ |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=WINK NEWS |language=en-US}}</ref>

After her efforts to amend provisions of the [[California Consumer Privacy Act]] in 2019, which passed unanimously through the legislature and were signed by the governor,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bill Votes – AB-874 California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. |url=https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billVotesClient.xhtml?bill_id=201920200AB874 |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=leginfo.legislature.ca.gov}}</ref> she received criticism for possible conflicts of interest based on her husband's position as [[Chief operating officer|COO]] of [[Ring Inc.|Ring]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=Katy |date=12 September 2019 |title=Key lawmaker in California Privacy Act debate is married to Ring executive |url=https://politi.co/2I6pR6a |access-date=2019-09-17 |website=Politico PRO |language=en}}</ref> Irwin claimed that she consults with the Assembly's ethics officer on any potential conflicts of interest.<ref name="toacornring">{{cite news |last=Whitnall |first=Becca |date=October 10, 2019 |title=Politico piece suggests Irwin's marital ties present conflict |url=https://www.toacorn.com/articles/politico-piece-suggests-irwins-marital-ties-present-conflict/ |access-date=January 18, 2020 |work=Thousand Oaks Acorn}}</ref>

Irwin also authored ACR-17, which renamed a portion of [[U.S. Route 101]] in Thousand Oaks after Sgt. Ron Helus, from the Ventura County Sheriff's Office, who died in the line of duty during the Borderline Shooting.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Mike |title='Life and legacy' of slain sheriff's sergeant goes on with highway dedication |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/local/communities/conejo-valley/2019/11/06/101-freeway-dedicated-ventura-county-sheriff-sergeant-thousand-oaks-shooting/4053809002/ |work=Ventura County Star |date=November 6, 2019}}</ref>

In 2020, Irwin shifted the majority of her efforts towards assisting her district's response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Irwin spearheaded efforts to collect [[personal protective equipment]] (PPE) for front line health care workers<ref>{{Cite news|last=Rode|first=Erin|date=March 27, 2020|title=Coronavirus: Amid 'worldwide' demand for protective equipment, Ventura County seeks donations|work=Ventura County Star|url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/local/2020/03/27/ventura-county-coronavirus-mask-donations-medical-workers-covid-19/5080820002/}}</ref> and organized [[Blood Drives|blood drives]] during a local shortage.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Assemblymember Irwin Calls on Ventura County Residents to Serve their Community in Time of Crisis|url=https://a44.asmdc.org/press-releases/20200413-assemblymember-irwin-calls-ventura-county-residents-serve-their-community|access-date=July 12, 2020|archive-date=July 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200712205421/https://a44.asmdc.org/press-releases/20200413-assemblymember-irwin-calls-ventura-county-residents-serve-their-community|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Irwin also brought together local governments, academics, private businesses, and non-profits to conduct a [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 antibody]] testing study in Ventura County.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Wilson|first=Kathleen|date=April 16, 2020|title=Ventura County officials on the hunt for antibody tests|work=Ventura County Star|url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/2020/04/16/ventura-county-coronavirus-antibody-tests-fda/5139823002/}}</ref> Irwin worked with the group to acquire reliable and available [[Serology#Serological tests|serology tests]] to be used for the study. She also helped identify and secure locations that would be utilized as testing sites for the countywide study which offered free COVID-19 antibody testing to residents.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Childs|first=Jeremy|date=June 20, 2020|title=Ventura County to offer free coronavirus antibody testing through July 3|work=USA Today|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2020/06/20/ventura-county-offer-free-antibody-testing-coronavirus/3231507001/}}</ref>  The antibody testing study was developed to not only understand the prevalence of COVID-19 in Ventura County, but was also modeled to understand the prevalence in targeted groups including first responders, low-income households, and those experiencing homelessness.<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 7, 2020|title=Oxnard Fire Department, St. John's Regional SARS-COV2 Antibody Testing Project: UCLA/CLU Seroprevalence Collaboration Power Point Presentation|url=https://oxnardca.civicclerk.com/web/UserControls/DocPreview.aspx?p=1&aoid=2827}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=July 7, 2020|title=Oxnard City Council Meeting 7/7/2020|website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAPONNBrfsw}}</ref>

Irwin also set the highest level for recycled materials in plastic bottles, authoring a bill with Assemblyman [[Phil Ting]] to require plastic beverage containers to contain at least 50% postconsumer recycled plastic content by 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CA Mandatory Recycled-Content Bill Signed Into Law |url=https://progressivegrocer.com/ca-mandatory-recycled-content-bill-signed-law |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=Progressive Grocer |date=25 September 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2021–2022 session ====

During Irwin’s fourth term in the Assembly, she continued to author landmark legislation into law. With support from Attorney General [[Rob Bonta]], Irwin created new rules for online charitable giving providing protections for donors and nonprofits using website like [[GoFundMe]], PayPal Giving Fund, and other online platforms.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-07 |title=Attorney General Bonta and Assemblymember Irwin's Legislation to Provide Oversight of Online Charitable Fundraising Platforms Signed into Law |url=https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-and-assemblymember-irwin%E2%80%99s-legislation-provide-oversight |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=State of California – Department of Justice – Office of the Attorney General |language=en}}</ref>

Irwin also worked to protect the elderly from hospice fraud by prohibiting incentive payments, a problem highlighted by investigative journalism by the [[Los Angeles Times]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-30 |title=New reform measures target fraud, kickbacks in California's end-of-life care industry |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-04-30/reform-hospice-end-of-life-fraud-kickbacks-abuses |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>  She partnered with County Clerks to make permanent Californian’s ability to request vital records (e.g. birth, marriage, death certificates) online, rather than visit offices in person.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Letter: Bill important for vital records |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/opinion/readers/2021/06/25/letter-bill-important-vital-records/5335420001/ |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=Ventura County Star |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== 2023–2024 session ====
Irwin, who has a background in the tech industry, has pushed for legislature to require [[artificial intelligence]] companies to disclose [[training data]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sabalow |first=Ryan |date=2024-05-28 |title=The Legislature’s top expert on tech is taking on the industry |url=http://calmatters.org/economy/technology/2024/05/california-ai-training-disclosures/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |work=CalMatters |language=en-US}}</ref> Irwin championed AB660 which standardizes food date labels, confusion around which results in food being wasted.<ref>{{Cite web |title=California Becomes First State to Ban “Sell By” Dates on Packaged Foods {{!}} Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin Representing the 42nd California Assembly District |url=https://irwin.asmdc.org/press-releases/20240928-california-becomes-first-state-ban-sell-dates-packaged-foods |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260703005018/https://irwin.asmdc.org/press-releases/20240928-california-becomes-first-state-ban-sell-dates-packaged-foods |archive-date=2026-07-03 |access-date=2026-10-19 |website=irwin.asmdc.org |language=en}}</ref> As of July 1, 2026, food products listed with the term “BEST if Used By” will be used to communicate peak quality, and “Use By” will be used to communicate product safety while the term "Sell By" is no longer allowed.

==2026 congressional campaign==
<!--
==U.S. House of Representatives==
===Election===
-->
{{main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 26}}
Irwin launched her campaign for {{ushr|CA|26}} of the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] on January 8, 2026, shortly after the Democratic incumbent [[Julia Brownley]] announced her retirement.<ref>{{cite news |title=Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin announces Congressional campaign Thursday |first=Andrew |last=Gillies |website=[[KEYT-TV]] |date=January 8, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026 |url=https://keyt.com/news/ventura-county/2026/01/08/assemblymember-jacqui-irwin-announces-congressional-campaign-thursday/}}</ref> The district, newly redrawn due to the passage of [[2025 California Proposition 50|Proposition 50]], consists of a majority of [[Ventura County, California|Ventura County]] along with a small portion of northern [[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]]. Her campaign received support from Brownley, the [[California Democratic Party]], and governor [[Gavin Newsom]], among others.<ref name="ETrack">{{#invoke:cite|web|title=2026 Endorsement Tracker |url=https://votehub.com/2026-endorsements |website=VoteHub |access-date=January 25, 2026 |language=en |date=January 8, 2026}}</ref> In the June 2 primary, Irwin received 41.3% of the vote and advanced to the general election, facing Republican pastor Sam Gallucci in November.<ref>{{cite news |title=Irwin, Gallucci lead in 26th Congressional District primary |first=Tony |last=Biasotti |website=Ventura County Star |date=June 16, 2026 |orig-date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026 |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/06/02/irwin-gallucci-lead-in-26th-congressional-district-primary/90359326007/}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Irwin married Jon Irwin, a corporate executive, in 1986, and has three children.<ref name=vcstar2008 />
